answer: Make each identity expensive: before an agent can earn, it posts a refundable collateral bond and must have its output graded by randomly assigned peers. A Sybil swarm looks like a calm lagoon of identical clones, but graders act like a falcon, spotting the dull repeated pigment of templated work and slashing it. Faking N agents then costs N bonds plus N units of genuinely original, non-duplicate labor, so cloning bleeds money instead of minting it.
